blocks.text: That קֹרֵא is the Damascene partridge, or Linnaeus' tetrao Israelitarum, described by Hasselquist, p. 331 ff., which the Arabs call Katta, قطا [qaṭā], from the sound it utters, is maintained by J. E. FABER on Harmar's Observatt. vol. 1, p. 305, note (SCHODER follows him in Specim. Hieroz. 2, Tit. 12), but with very flimsy arguments, which I forbear to review, since they have already been sufficiently refuted by Oedmann, p. 55.
